memory_update.text: MYRG should be retained for deeper Layer 2 work as a cleaner underfollowed electrical construction/T&D contractor with explicit backlog and utility grid exposure.

PRIM should be retained as a mixed but relevant utility services contractor where the key diligence question is whether power delivery is becoming a durable margin and backlog driver versus gas/communications/renewables cyclicality.

NVEE is a speculative-shadow candidate for the engineering, commissioning, substation design, utility coordination, and inspection layer; exposure appears real but may be too small or too diversified without segment-level confirmation.
The investable chokepoint for this node appears to split into two subnodes: craft-skilled field construction capacity and technical commissioning/design/inspection capacity.

Vegetation-management exposure remains difficult to map to US-listed equities because major players such as Asplundh and Davey are private; future passes should search for public roll-ups, utility O&M contractors, herbicide suppliers, LiDAR/geospatial inspection vendors, and storm-response subcontractors.

node: Grid EPC subcontractors, utility field services, testing, commissioning, maintenance, vegetation management, and specialized labor
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the public-market map around grid field execution capacity rather than obvious power equipment. The reference anchor is Quanta Services, but the more relevant discovery lane is smaller electrical contractors and engineering/testing firms with transmission, distribution, substation, power-delivery, commissioning, and utility customer exposure. The main underfollowed angle is that grid capex can be bottlenecked by qualified field crews, utility-approved contractors, commissioning specialists, interconnection/substation engineering, and recurring maintenance work, not only by transformers, breakers, or conductors.
